📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:25.

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw across seven games in all competitions, Aston Villa have failed to come out on top in any of their last four matches (D2 L2), with their latest setback sparking a furious reaction from manager Unai Emery.

Villa allowed Man United to come from two goals behind twice and salvage a point in a chaotic 4-4 draw at Old Trafford prior to the international break, with the visitors conceding two goals in stoppage time to be denied what would have been just their third win at the Theatre of Dreams in 32 visits.

Three wins, four draws and three defeats have been posted by the Midlands club in 10 top-flight games this term, leaving them sitting 10th in the Premier League table and five points behind the top four where they finished last season.

Since the beginning of October, Villa have dropped a joint-division-high six points from winning positions, while their defensive concerns remain having conceded in 13 of their 16 matches across all competitions this season.

Heading into Emery’s 150th Premier League game in charge this weekend, Villa have found the net 14 times across a five-game unbeaten home run (W3 D2), while they have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight meetings with Sunderland (W5 D6) – a 3-1 away defeat in January 2016.

Sunderland ended a miserable seven-game winless run in the Premier League with a much-needed 1-0 triumph over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light before the international break, courtesy of a first-half penalty from Enzo Le Fee.

Head coach Regis Le Bris was delighted to see his Black Cats side ‘re-connect with our identity and our fans’ after delivering a gritty and disciplined display that helped them climb off the foot of the Premier League table for the first time in three weeks.

Now sitting 19th and only three points behind Hull in 13th spot, Sunderland will be looking to win consecutive top-flight games for the first time this season when they make the trip to Villa Park this weekend, as well as end their five-game winless streak on the road.

The Black Cats sit rock bottom of the away form table having accumulated only one point (D1 L4) and conceded a joint-division-high 13 goals, including three in a 3-1 defeat at Coventry City at the end of last month.

Sunderland now head to the Midlands seeking to end a seven-game winless run away against Aston Villa across all competitions (D3 L4), with their last victory at Villa Park coming in January 2011 when Phil Bardsley’s late strike secured a 1-0 Premier League triumph under Steve Bruce.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana – who signed a contract extension earlier this week – and Matteo Ruggeri both remain sidelined through injury, while Matty Cash is also out after picking up concussion on international duty with Poland.

In a recent development, however, Johan Manzambi is available for selection after recovering from a calf matter, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka should also be ready to play after missing the last six games with a thigh injury. He could therefore compete with Taylor Harwood-Bellis for the right-back berth.

Nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and Alysson were all on the scoresheet at Old Trafford and will hope to retain their starting spots in the final third. Leon Goretzka also scored against Man United but he faces competition from Joao Gomes to start in centre-midfield alongside Boubacar Kamara.

As for Sunderland, Le Bris has confirmed that captain Granit Xhaka (calf) and striker Brian Brobbey (thigh) are ruled out due to injury, joining Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard and Habib Diarra (both thigh) in the treatment room.

However, Omar Alderete is back from a one-match suspension and could replace Luke O'Nein at centre-back, joining Trai Hume, Nordi Mukiele and Reinildo Mandava in defence.

Chemsdine Talbi was handed his first PL start of the season against Chelsea and will hope to continue on the left flank ahead of Nilson Angulo, while Wilson Isidor – who scored home and away against Villa last season – is set to lead the line in Brobbey's absence.

Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan Futuro decided to go in a upcoming direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?
  • Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan Futuro decided to go in a upcoming direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Sources indicate that things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

It has been revealed that with promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Industry observers note that under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

Sources indicate that this also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

It has been revealed that similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most vital aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.
  • The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13.

In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.

The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.

Blackpool return to action on Saturday fresh off the dismissal of manager Evatt with the hopes of climbing away from the League One drop zone.

They endured a tough start to their first full campaign under Evatt, right now sitting 20th with just 12 points on the board from 13 games, winning three and losing seven of those.

The most recent of those victories came in October to end a six-game winless run in the third tier, but the Tangerines failed to build on it, going on to lose 4-1 to Mansfield and rescue a 1-1 draw against a Sheffield Wednesday side who played the second half with 10 men.

Then after scraping past non-league AFC Hornchurch in extra time in the FA Cup first round, they visited AFC Wimbledon last weekend and again came away empty-handed, having failed to find a leveller after Alistair Smith's 13th-minute.

That triggered the dismissal of Evatt by the club hierarchy on Thursday, and now under the temporary charge of Steve Thompson and only above the relegation zone on goal difference, they will be desperate to begin rebuilding confidence and a cushion over the bottom four with a much-needed home win.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to continue an upturn in form and their climb away from the relegation zone.

Wigan Athletic also endured a tough start to their League One campaign under Gary Caldwell, sitting bottom after 12 games with just seven points on the board having lost nine of those matches.

That was largely down to the Latics' struggles in attack, but they appear to have turned a corner since, winning two and drawing one of their last three league games while scoring five goals, firstly ending a three-game losing run by beating fellow strugglers Bromley 3-2.

Then following a stalemate with Mansfield Town and consecutive cup wins over Boreham Wood and Crewe Alexandra, Caldwell's men went into another important contest at home to Barnsley on Saturday and won 2-1 as Fraser Murray put them ahead, Cameron McGeehan pegged them back and Jensen Weir scored the decisive goal 15 minutes from time.

Still with plenty of cause for concern in their away record, having drawn one and lost six of seven league games on the road, but finally with some momentum on their side, Wigan Athletic head to Bloomfield Road in search of a third win in four games to build on their two-point lead over the drop zone.

Wigan Athletic League One form:.

Wigan Athletic form (all competitions):.

Blackpool were hit by a sickness bug for last weekend's game, with Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe among those to miss out.

They may be back in contention for Saturday, while defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe remain sidelined alongside George Honeyman.

Karoy Anderson will head back from international duty with Jamaica but was in action in Mexico on Wednesday, while Dion Charles, Jerry Yates, CJ Hamilton and Niall Ennis will all compete for attacking places after Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham partnered up up top last time out.

Wigan Athletic will likely remain without forwards Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris due to ongoing injuries.

Scott Hogan is back in contention after a brief layoff and came off the bench last time out, but Caldwell may go unchanged from the Barnsley win, with Christian Saydee leading the line with support from Bradley Burrowes and Jon Mellish.

Murray will continue to offer attacking support in a wing-back role after his opener against Barnsley, while Weir and Max Power will continue in the middle of a 3-4-3 setup.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Southwood; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Niskanen, Morgan, Brown, Coulson; Bowler, Charles, Yates.

Wigan Athletic possible starting lineup:.

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, Murray; Burrowes, Mellish; Saydee.

Blackpool remain devoid of confidence and have been hit by injuries, illness and a managerial departure, but they still have more quality than their league standing suggests while the visitors have been poor away from home this season.

We see the Tangerines at least avoiding defeat against a resurgent Wigan team.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.
  • Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.
  • Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40.

Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.

Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.

A 10-match winless run between August 8 and October 23 dampened any optimism that may have been brewing after Telstar’s season-opening win over NEC. However, they have since responded with four points from a possible six, most recently earning a 2-2 draw against Fortuna Sittard.

Having been tipped by many as the next managerial casualty of 2026-27, Henk Brugge appears to have bought himself some breathing room, but he will know his position remains precarious, and any underwhelming result could still spell the end for him.

Averaging two goals per home league match this term, De Witte Leeuwen have found little difficulty scoring in front of their fans, although much of that good work is being undone by a porous defence that has conceded 17 times across six home games.

January’s 4-1 defeat marked Telstar’s seventh straight loss against Zwolle and extended their winless run in this fixture to 16 matches across all competitions dating back to February 2007. This weekend’s hosts will need to buck an unpleasant trend to secure all three points.

A 4-2 triumph over FC Utrecht in their most recent home match ended a run of six games without a win for Telstar, who now seek back-to-back victories in Velsen for the first time since beating Sparta Rotterdam and Heracles by a combined score of 7-1 to close out 2025-26 on a high.

In a recent development, after weeks of searching, PEC Zwolle will have a new face in the dugout for their upcoming clash against Telstar, with Alex Pastoor recently appointed as head coach until the end of the 2026-27 season. He replaces Henry van der Vegt, whose 15-month tenure ended in October.

Pastoor’s immediate task will be to build on his side’s four-game league unbeaten run, during which they have collected eight points from a possible 12, with only Heerenveen (12) and Ajax (10) boasting a better record in the division.

With three of their next four matches coming against teams at the moment in the top seven - AZ Alkmaar, Fortuna Sittard, and PSV Eindhoven - De Blauwvingers could use a win here as they look to put some distance between themselves and the drop zone before the end of 2026.

Both of Saturday’s opponents have managed just three clean sheets between them from 24 matches this season, so this weekend’s clash is likely to be decided at the attacking end. On that front, Zwolle have struggled compared to their hosts, scoring five fewer goals so far.

However, the visitors could tilt things in their favour with a quick start, and having scored the opener in four of the last five gameweeks, they may look to capitalise on a Telstar side that has conceded first four times during that span.

Telstar form (all competitions):.

PEC Zwolle form (all competitions):.

Gerald Alders, 21, has missed Telstar’s last four matches and will remain sidelined for Saturday’s clash as he continues his recovery to full fitness.

Rui Mendes is also unlikely to feature for the hosts, though his comeback is not far off after missing the last three matches.

Tyrone Owusu has four goals and one assist in his last six outings, already making this his most productive season in a Telstar shirt.

Deadline-day loan signing Filip Krastev has yet to feature this term due to an Achilles tendon injury sustained while playing for Goztepe.

Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus are also unavailable this weekend, but both are nearing their respective returns.

Telstar possible starting lineup:.

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Ahmed, Rossen; Martha, Owusu, Brouwer; Thorisson.

PEC Zwolle possible starting lineup:.

Schendelaar; Van der Haar, Viergever, Velthuis, Aertssen; Sommer, Thomas; Mbayo, Namli, Van der Wal; Van Hooijdonk.

Both teams have performed well of late, and neither enters Saturday’s game with their confidence depleted.

With little to separate the sides, a draw appears the most likely outcome, so we are backing a share of the spoils.

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

Recent findings suggest that as La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the upcoming busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Sources indicate that despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby reveals, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

In a recent development, moreira is at the moment captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

It has been revealed that amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

According to recent reports, with four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

In a recent development, if left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

In a recent development, 'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:39.

Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.

The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino officially started work as Red Devils head coach on Wednesday, having flown straight to England after managing his final USA game against Haiti.

The South American has taken charge of a team that right now sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up just eight points from their first 10 games of the season.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free," Pochettino told Man United's official website.

Industry observers note that “The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most notable thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

"When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero. I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.

In a recent development, “To create the culture is the most vital [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create. We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.

“The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players.

According to recent reports, "We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”.

Pochettino's training session on Thursday included both Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu, with the defensive duo both in line to be available against Liverpool.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

Recent findings suggest that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant said: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a significant game again on Tuesday so it’s notable to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

It has been revealed that “We’ve had a great week. A new manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

Recent findings suggest that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

It has been revealed that “I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

According to recent reports, how has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A newly introduced-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most important thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

Recent findings suggest that “I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

“We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Industry observers note that scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his upcoming role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

Swansea City must make homegrown quota a priority to allow 30-year-old striker more game-time: Opinion

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, swansea City have had an excellent start to this season.
  • Recent findings suggest that ross Stewart’s Swansea City career has already presented an unusual contradiction.
  • Sources indicate that the Scotland international, who featured at the 2026 World Cup, arrived as a free-agent signing with a proven goalscoring record.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, swansea City have had an excellent start to this season. However, they have had some concerns, one of which has severely hampered a summer signings ability to make his mark in South Wales.

Recent findings suggest that ross Stewart’s Swansea City career has already presented an unusual contradiction. The striker scored on his first start, helping then Vitor Matos’s side secure a 4-0 victory over Blackburn Rovers, but has since been restricted to around 171 minutes across five Championship appearances.

Sources indicate that the Scotland international, who featured at the 2026 World Cup, arrived as a free-agent signing with a proven goalscoring record. However, his opportunities have been limited by the EFL’s homegrown rules. Scottish players do not count towards the requirement for seven qualifying players in a matchday squad.

It means a proven Championship striker is competing against administrative constraints as well as his fellow forwards. Swansea must decide whether they are overlooking a valuable attacking option or whether caution is justified given his injury record.

Industry observers note that EFL rules require clubs to include at least seven homegrown players in their matchday squads. To qualify, players must have been registered with an English or Welsh club for three years before their 21st birthday. Stewart’s development in Scottish football means he does not meet those criteria.

Injuries to other qualifying players, alongside summer sales and loans involving academy products, have made the situation particularly challenging for the Swans.

Stewart has managed one goal from 171 minutes for Swansea this season, equivalent to approximately 0.53 goals per 90. His expected goals figure stands at 1.80, suggesting he has not yet fully capitalised on his opportunities. However, the sample size is too small to draw firm conclusions.

His aerial ability, finishing and hold-up play also offer Swansea a different attacking dimension.

Industry observers note that there is, however, a legitimate argument for remaining cautious. Stewart’s career has been interrupted by several significant injuries, particularly during his Southampton spell, while another early-season concern has disrupted his start at Swansea.

At 30, durability is an vital consideration. His goalscoring record when available is impressive, but Swansea cannot overlook the possibility that increasing his workload could create further fitness problems. Matos also has alternative attacking options.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, the homegrown requirement should not become an unnecessary obstacle to using one of Swansea’s most proven finishers. January provides an opportunity to address the problem by recruiting another qualifying player and giving Matos greater selection flexibility.

Sources indicate that stewart’s injury history makes caution understandable, but his Championship record suggests there is still considerable value in giving him a proper opportunity. Swansea should find a structural solution rather than allow their regulations to dictate how often one of their most experienced attackers can feature.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 20:03, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:05.

Fulham are reportedly working to extend Calvin Bassey's contract amid interest from Manchester United.

The Red Devils are expected to bring a centre-back to Old Trafford in the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

Man United are planning to overhaul their defensive unit next summer, as Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are all out of contract, while there is speculation surrounding the futures of Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

However, due to the team's severe defensive problems this term, it is likely that a new centre-back will be targeted when the winter window opens for business.

Man United have conceded 19 times in their 10 Premier League matches this season, which is the joint-third worst record in the division.

The Red Devils have actually not kept a single clean sheet in the Premier League this term, while they have also conceded eight times in their four Champions League matches.

Bassey has allegedly been identified by Man United as a leading target, with the 26-year-old's contract due to expire at the end of the campaign.

Fulham do have the option to activate another year on the Nigeria international's deal, but the club are looking to sign him to a long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, Fulham are currently pushing to extend his deal, with the London team having no intention of letting him leave in the winter market.

Bassey has captained Fulham this season, making 12 appearances in 2026-27, while he has represented the club on 113 occasions in all competitions.

The defender has also played for Rangers and Ajax during his professional career.

Bassey gained Champions League experience during his time at Ajax, while he has now played 104 times in the Premier League for Fulham, scoring three goals and registering one assist.

New Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed with funds during the January transfer window.

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

Recent findings suggest that “That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial problem,” he began.

Sources indicate that “Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

According to recent reports, “But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

According to recent reports, “Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”.

Man City midfielder tipped for free transfer exit as preferred destinations emerge

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 20:47.
  • Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.
  • Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an update on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 20:47.

Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an update on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.

Speaking to Marca, Moretto claimed that the 32-year-old would welcome a return to Spain or Italy, where he previously represented Real Madrid and Inter Milan respectively.

"He will leave City at the end of the season," Moretto noted, before explaining that Kovacic "would like to return to Spain or Italy", although his salary expectations could influence his options.

The patch comes as Kovacic struggles to secure regular playing time under Enzo Maresca, having fallen down the midfield pecking order since the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola.

While City have not officially confirmed his departure, the midfielder is approaching the final seven months of his contract without a reported agreement over an extension.

Kovacic joined Manchester City from Chelsea in June 2023, signing a four-year contract in a deal worth an initial £25m, with a further £5m potentially payable in add-ons.

The Croatia international was recruited to provide experience, technical quality and composure in midfield, having previously enjoyed considerable success with both Real Madrid and Chelsea.

However, injuries have increasingly disrupted his time in Manchester.

The midfielder was restricted to just nine appearances during the 2025-26 campaign after undergoing surgery to address a troublesome heel problem.

Although he has returned to action this season, his opportunities have remained limited under Maresca.

Kovacic has made eight appearances across all competitions, contributing one goal and one assist, but only one of those outings has been a Premier League start.

He has also been used sparingly in the Champions League, with the manager preferring other midfield options for the majority of City's European fixtures.

His two full appearances in the EFL Cup underline the change in his status, although he was entrusted with the captain's armband in one of those matches.

The situation represents a considerable shift for a player who has won four Champions League titles and previously played an crucial role in some of Europe's most successful teams.

Reports linking Kovacic with an exit have circulated for several months.

In September, the Croatian was reportedly considering a January departure after becoming frustrated with his lack of opportunities.

Moretto's latest information, however, points towards a summer move when Kovacic would become available without a transfer fee.

From January, the midfielder will be eligible to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with clubs outside England, potentially allowing him to arrange his next destination before the end of the campaign.

Kovacic's reported preference for Spain or Italy would represent a return to familiar surroundings rather than an entirely fresh challenge.

The midfielder spent two seasons with Inter Milan before joining Real Madrid in 2015, where he won three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018.

He subsequently moved to Chelsea, initially on loan, and spent five seasons at Stamford Bridge before completing his switch to City.

His experience in Serie A has already attracted attention from Italian clubs.

Juventus were linked with a move for Kovacic in September, when reports suggested that the Turin giants had identified him as one of several potential free-agent signings for the summer of 2027.

The Bianconeri were also remarked to be monitoring Fikayo Tomori and David Raum as part of their efforts to strengthen the squad without paying substantial transfer fees.

AC Milan have separately been mentioned among Kovacic's possible suitors, although there is no indication that either Italian club has reached an agreement with the player.

The possibility of returning to La Liga also remains open, but Moretto's comments did not identify a Spanish club presently negotiating for his signature.

His wages could prove the biggest obstacle to a move.

Despite the prospect of securing an accomplished international without paying City a transfer fee, interested clubs would still need to reach an agreement over a salary package acceptable to Kovacic.

For City, the latest update raises the prospect of losing another member of Guardiola's former midfield without receiving a transfer fee.

Maresca's current selection decisions suggest that Kovacic is no longer regarded as an automatic starter, although the Croatian remains part of the squad and has not publicly confirmed any looks to leave.

With his contract due to expire next June, the coming months could determine whether he completes his final season in Manchester or attracts an offer to bring forward his departure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:24.

Eyeing up a place in the top four of the Premier League, in-form Bournemouth welcome Nottingham Forest to the Vitality Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The spoils were shared in the last meeting between these two teams in May, with an opener from Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White cancelled out in the second half by Cherries attacker Marcus Tavernier to rescue a 1-1 draw.

Bournemouth’s 2026-27 campaign started with just two wins in eight matches across all competitions (D3 L3), including no victories in six Premier League fixtures, but the Cherries have since put together an impressive eight-game winning streak under fresh boss Marco Rose.

A slender 2-1 success at Ipswich Town prior to the international break helped them climb up to seventh in the Premier League table, just three points behind Liverpool in fourth, and they are now aiming to win five straight top-flight games for the first time in their history.

Since the start of October, Bournemouth have scored more goals across all competitions than any other Premier League team (22), netting at least two goals in each game during their eight-match winning run.

In a recent development, in-form striker Evanilson has been Bournemouth's driving force, with the Brazilian’s goal against Ipswich making him the first Cherries player to score in five successive PL matches. He also has the joint-most top-flight goal involvements this season (nine - five goals, four assists), level with Erling Haaland (nine goals).

Not only do Bournemouth enter Saturday’s contest having never lost in eight previous Premier League battles with Nottingham Forest (W4 D4), but Rose has also won his last four meetings with teams managed by Oliver Glasner (all in the Bundesliga between 2021 and 2023).

After enduring a sluggish start to life under Glasner, winning just one of their first nine Premier League games, Nottingham Forest entered the international break on a massive high after securing a statement 3-1 victory over Manchester City at the City Ground – their first home league win of the campaign.

Liam Delap ended a five-game goal drought with a superb brace against his former club that followed an earlier opener from Jair Cunha, with Forest scoring more goals in this match (three) than they had in their previous six home league fixtures combined (two).

Sitting 16th in the Premier League table and one point above the drop zone, Forest must now translate that momentum onto their travels, having failed to keep an away clean sheet in the top flight since April while losing their last two games on the road against Crystal Palace (3-1) and Brentford (2-0).

Although Forest have scored the second-fewest goals in the division this term (nine), Glasner – who takes charge of his 100th Premier League match on Saturday – will hope that his team’s clinical display against Man City signals a turning point after weeks of frustration in front of goal.

The Tricky Trees head to the Vitality Stadium seeking to win back-to-back league games for only the second time this calendar year, but they are winless in six away league encounters against Bournemouth (D2 L4).

Bournemouth Premier League form:.

Bournemouth form (all competitions):.

Nottingham Forest Premier League form:.

Bournemouth duo Alex Toth (thigh) and Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) remain sidelined with injuries, while Julian Araujo is still nursing a thigh problem and is unlikely to be involved this weekend.

Rayan sustained a knock on international duty with Brazil, but the winger should be fit to start on the right side of attack, linking up with Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier and red-hot centre-forward Evanilson.

Eli Junior Kroupi is another attacking option pushing to start having made a full recovery from injury and scoring his first goal for France last weekend, while in-demand midfielder Alex Scott is available to start for the first time since suffering a thigh injury with England in October.

As for Nottingham Forest, Nicolas Dominguez (hamstring) remains a long-term absentee and has been joined in the treatment room by Callum Hudson-Odoi (groin), while Neco Williams (ankle) and Xaver Schlager (thigh) have both emerged as doubts after picking up injuries with Wales and Austria respectably over the international break.

According to recent reports, nicolo Savona is yet to play for Forest this season due to a knee injury, but he is back training and may be in a position to return to the matchday squad. A start is seemingly unlikely, though, with Daniel Munoz and either Williams - if fit - or Luca Netz expected to start as wing-backs.

Delap is bidding to score in successive PL games for the first time since April 2025 with Ipswich and is expected to lead the line once again, with Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye potentially providing support in advanced positions; the latter’s inclusion would allow James McAtee to move back into a deeper midfield position.

Bournemouth possible starting lineup:.

Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Cook; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:.

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Delap.

Both Bournemouth and Forest enter this contest in buoyant mood as they look to build on positive results prior to the international break.

Although six of Forest's last seven Premier League away games have seen both teams score, we are backing the Cherries to frustrate an opponent they have historically enjoyed facing and secure three more points without reply to extend their impressive winning run to nine matches.

Industry observers note that southampton had a mixed summer transfer window but one major blow was the sale of Taylor Harwood-Bellis. The Saints brought in multiple defenders in a bid to replace him and one of which was Zach Abbott who joined on loan.

Abbott has since struggled for gametime and fellow summer signing Keven Schlotterbeck has impressed but is now out injured. With that in mind, Tonda Eckert may may be hoping to bring in another centre-back during the January window.

Sources indicate that southampton are in an excellent position to push for automatic promotion this season, something that they cannot afford to take any risks with. With that in mind, they should be keeping an eye on Torbjorn Heggem’s situation.

In a recent development, the former West Brom man looks likely to leave Bologna this January, sparking talk of a return to the Baggies. However, while talk of a move to the Hawthorns has been quashed, a move to Southampton should be under consideration.

The 27-year-old has struggled for regular opportunities under Raffaele Palladino and has made it clear that he does not want to spend the remainder of the season sitting on the bench.

With the January transfer window approaching, the Saints could have an opportunity to bring an established international back to English football.

Industry observers note that heggem joined Bologna from West Brom in August 2025 after an impressive Championship campaign. He has since made 45 appearances for the Serie A side, but his involvement has decreased this season. That could leave Southampton well placed to explore a deal.

It has been revealed that the Norwegian international has already demonstrated his ability to perform in the Championship. During the 2024/25 campaign, he made 45 league appearances for West Brom, scoring once and providing two assists. His consistency earned him both the Players’ Player of the Season and Supporters’ Player of the Season awards, underlining how highly regarded he was at The Hawthorns.

Industry observers note that heggem offers physical presence, aerial ability and impressive distribution. He is naturally a centre-back but can also operate at left-back, while his preference for his left foot makes him an especially useful defensive option.

Sources indicate that his current Serie A statistics also demonstrate his technical qualities. Across seven appearances and 525 minutes this season, he has completed 93.4 per cent of his passes, recorded 43 line-breaking passes and made 27 clearances. He has also won 12 aerial duels and earned 25 caps for Norway.

In a recent development, southampton would face competition for his signature, and his wages could prove a stumbling block. Nevertheless, he is approaching his prime, has proven himself in the Championship and possesses experience at a higher level.

It has been revealed that with promotion ambitions potentially shaping their January business, Southampton should seriously consider swooping for Heggem. He could be an outstanding addition to their defensive options.

Legendary commentator MARTIN TYLER on taking the Premier League plunge in 1992, Arsene Wenger's fury, his love of Woking - and THAT Sergio Aguero moment

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.
  • Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the fresh satellite channel.

'A new frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a big town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

It has been revealed that 'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

The Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always stated you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he notes, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Industry observers note that tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he states. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

In a recent development, 'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

Sources indicate that his manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s company is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

Recent findings suggest that and he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' notes Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

It has been revealed that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' says Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he claims. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

Sources indicate that the range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

According to recent reports, it is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

Sheffield United are having the last laugh over £6m Burnley deal

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following the sales of Andre Brooks, Callum O’Hare, and Gustavo Hamer in the summer, Sheffield United appeared to be in a spot of bother, especially with parachute payments running out.
  • The Blades had no choice but to rely solely on loans and free transfers, bringing in the likes of Ben Brereton Diaz, Romelle Donovan, Jordan Ayew, and Matt Doherty to subdued fanfare.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United endured a tricky start to the Championship campaign, but Chris Wilder’s side have fought their way up the table in recent weeks and are having the last laugh regarding one transfer saga.

Following the sales of Andre Brooks, Callum O’Hare, and Gustavo Hamer in the summer, Sheffield United appeared to be in a spot of bother, especially with parachute payments running out.

The Blades had no choice but to rely solely on loans and free transfers, bringing in the likes of Ben Brereton Diaz, Romelle Donovan, Jordan Ayew, and Matt Doherty to subdued fanfare.

With almost no money to spend, Chris Wilder’s side saw themselves priced out of numerous deals, including one that would have reunited a former fan favourite with Bramall Lane.

Sheffield United were interested in bringing Bosnian centre-back Anel Ahmedhodzic back to the club over the summer, after Feyenoord made it abundantly clear that they were looking to sell the 27-year-old.

Ahmedhodzic initially joined the Blades in the summer of 2022 from French outfit Bordeaux, and across the next three years, he would make 114 appearances across all competitions for the South Yorkshire outfit, including 31 in the Premier League.

After Sheffield United were defeated in the 2025 Championship play-off final by Sunderland, Ahmedhodzic, along with the likes of Vinicius Souza and Kieffer Moore, left the club the following summer, with the Bosnian heading to Rotterdam to link up with Feyenoord.

However, after just one year at De Kuip and 36 appearances across all competitions, the defender was made available for transfer this summer, but it rapidly became apparent that the Blades could not afford him, as a division rival swooped in under their noses.

Following their relegation from the Premier League and departures of Maxime Esteve, Joe Worrall, and Axel Tuanzebe, Burnley were in the market for defensive reinforcements.

Then under Nicky Hayen, the Clarets completed deals for Max Alleyne, Igor Julio, and Ahmedhodzic, with the latter heading to Turf Moor in a deal worth around £6 million.

It was viewed as a real coup for Burnley at the time, with Ahmedhodzic having ample Championship experience under his belt and at a decent age, but so far, he has struggled to justify that fee.

Amid Burnley’s struggles, the Bosnian has not helped stop the rot spreading in Lancashire, with the Clarets sitting in the relegation zone after 15 league games with just one win, and, with just six league appearances, he has found himself on the bench and out of the squad entirely in recent weeks.

Certainly, this is not how he would’ve imagined his return to England going, as those at Bramall Lane must be laughing.

With Ahmedhodzic joining Burnley, this didn’t stop Sheffield United’s own pursuit of defensive reinforcements, as with a deal for Leicester City’s Harry Souttar looking too expensive, Wilder turned to the loan market.

Coventry City centre-back Liam Kitching, following the Sky Blues’ promotion to the top flight, found himself out of Frank Lampard’s prepares at the CBS Arena, and Wilder moved quickly to secure a deal for the Irishman.

Following his late move to South Yorkshire, Kitching has been an almost ever-present in the Blades’ back line alongside Japhet Tanganga, with ten league appearances so far, and reminding everyone why he was a crucial cog in Coventry’s promotion to the Premier League.

Having not paid a penny for Kitching, Sheffield United and Wilder must be laughing now after Ahmedhodzic's struggles with Burnley, as an expensive transfer bullet may have been dodged.

Sources indicate that would you have liked to have seen Anel Ahmedhodzic return to Sheffield United in the summer, or are you happy with Liam Kitching? Share your thoughts below!

With Burnley and Ahmedhodzic struggling at the foot of the Championship table and Sheffield United within touching distance of the play-offs, Wilder will surely be pleased with the way things have panned out.

Of course, had the Bosnian returned to Bramall Lane, then things could have gone differently, and he could be a key part of the side in South Yorkshire now.

But avoiding a £6 million fee and signing someone some people will argue is better, the Blades have come out on the right end of this saga, much to Burnley’s dismay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 21:02, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 21:05.

Two teams that have enjoyed solid starts to their respective 2026-27 La Liga campaigns will lock horns on Saturday, with Alaves hosting Deportivo La Coruna.

The visitors have been one of the surprise packages of the season thus far following their promotion from the second tier last term.

Alaves boast a record of three wins, four draws and five defeats from their 12 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with 13 points leaving them in 12th spot in the La Liga table.

The Blue and Whites drew 0-0 with Sevilla in their last league match, but they thumped Anaitasuna FT 6-1 in the Copa del Rey last time out to secure a position in round two.

Quique Sanchez Flores's side have not managed to triumph in the league since the start of September, but it has still been a strong start to the campaign given that they were 14th last term, only avoiding relegation by a single point.

Alaves have won 20, lost 18 and drawn 11 of their previous 49 matches against Deportivo, and the last two games between the two sides have ended in victories for the Basque outfit.

The Glorious One recorded a 1-0 win over Deportivo when the two teams last locked horns in Spain's top flight, which came in February 2018.

Deportivo secured promotion back to La Liga courtesy of their second-placed finish in last season's Segunda Division, and it has been a successful return to this level of football.

Antonio Hidalgo's side have a record of three wins, six draws and three defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 15 points leaving them in ninth spot in the division.

The Blue and Whites have won two and drawn one of their last three matches, entering the November international break off the back of a 0-0 with Espanyol.

Deportivo have actually only lost one of their last five games in all competitions, while they have picked up six points from their six away matches in La Liga this season.

Alaves will once again be missing Facundo Garces and Mikel Rodriguez through injury, but the home side are otherwise in strong shape for their clash with Deportivo.

Lucas Boye has been in strong form this season, scoring five times in 11 appearances, and the 30-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be an introduction into the team for Mariano Diaz, who has come up with six goals and five assists in 13 appearances during the current campaign.

As for Deportivo, Bright Ede and Zakaria Eddahchouri are both expected to be unavailable for selection due to injury problems.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has now made two appearances off the bench after recovering from an injury, and the experienced attacker could now come back into the starting XI.

Luisimi Cruz has scored twice in 13 appearances this season and is also expected to feature in the starting side, while there should also be a position for Yeremay Hernandez.
