💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday.
  • Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu.
  • Summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, blackburn Rovers face Burnley in a Lancashire derby on Sunday. It’s a massive occasion at Ewood Park, not only because of the rivalry, but because it marks Rovers’ first game since Tony Mowbray stepped back as head coach due to health challenges earlier this week.

Industry observers note that damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will lead the side on an interim basis, but the temporary bosses will not be able to call upon star right-back Ryan Alebiosu. The Nigerian international has undergone surgery on his knee and is set to be sidelined until the New Year.

Summer signing Gady Beyuku replaced Alebiosu when he hobbled off against Stoke City. And, he played the full 90 minutes against West Ham while the medical staff waited for a verdict on Alebiosu’s blow.

Now that we know how long Blackburn Rovers’ go-to right-back will be out for, Beyuku has a real chance to make the starting role his own.

Most clubs have at least two players to cover in every position, and that is the case at Blackburn Rovers. With Alebiosu out, Beyuku is the only natural senior right-back available for selection, paving the way for him to come into the side.

A reported fee of around £1.2m was paid to sign the 20-year-old from Modena in the summer, so there is clear belief in his potential. It was widely expected that Beyuku would be cover and competition for Alebiosu, but the injury thrusts him into the limelight.

He’s shown signs of growing into Championship football early on as well. His second-half against West Ham was the best we’ve seen from Beyuku to date, offering a lively presence up and down the right-hand side.

In a recent development, the Frenchman saw to his duties at the back with 10 defensive contributions, but he was forward-thinking and frequently involved in possession like Alebiosu as well. Beyuku completed 26 of his 29 passes, nine of which were line-breaking.

He was dispossessed twice, but this does come with the territory of being a progressive right-back who is still developing and settling into a latest league (all stats via FotMob).

In a recent development, alebiosu’s shoes are major ones to fill. It might not have been planned that Beyuku would assume a starting role this early into his Blackburn Rovers, given his age and need to grow into Championship football.

It means that, despite the fact he needs to deliver, there should be an element of patience.

According to recent reports, if Johnson and Dodds feel Beyuku needs to be taken out of the side, there are options to consider. Kristi Montgomery has a key role in midfield alongside Sam Morsy but he has covered at right-back before. Matty Litherland is working his way back from injury too, while Lewis Miller is a longer-term absentee.

According to recent reports, beyuku will have the firm backing of the Rovers faithful. A strong display against arch-rivals Burnley this Sunday would be a sure-fire way for the youngster to endear himself to the fans and announce himself in Championship football.

#72732. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6428 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

That may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

It has been revealed that on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

Industry observers note that it could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

In a recent development, kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

The irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

The manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

According to recent reports, it was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Sources indicate that maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Sources indicate that now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Industry observers note that then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

It could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

Recent findings suggest that ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was promptly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

Industry observers note that how Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Sources indicate that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel mentioned. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

It has been revealed that “We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team indicated up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We revealed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

Industry observers note that “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon says mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

In a recent development, A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

England have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

In a recent development, then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

Baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

Recent findings suggest that garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

It has been revealed that double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

Industry observers note that saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

According to recent reports, the way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Sources indicate that baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

Guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

Industry observers note that england are making a double change as Garner and Rogers come on for Lewis-Skelly and Gordon. Garner was not in the initial squad but takes his chance now after the withdrawals.

Spain also make a substitution as Pedri replaces Ruiz.

At one end, Yamal has a shot blocked after England gave the ball away before Lewis-Skelly’s shot down the other end is easily saved.

Sources indicate that “This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

It has been revealed that england’s looks for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

According to recent reports, “He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel said. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

“For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

According to recent reports, declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against Newly introduced Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

Latest Update: Celtic & Southampton must be feeling fresh Stoke City transfer regret

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stoke City headed into the international break level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough at the top of the Championship table, as Mark Robins will be looking to ensure his side can maintain this form upon their return to action.
  • Indeed, only Birmingham’s and Middlesbrough’s superior goal difference keeps Stoke off the top of the Championship table right now as things stand, with the Potters enjoying another excellent start to the campaign.
  • It was around this time last year when Stoke suffered a calamitous dip in form, as Robins must be doing everything he can to avoid a similar fate this time around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City headed into the international break level on points with Birmingham City and Middlesbrough at the top of the Championship table, as Mark Robins will be looking to ensure his side can maintain this form upon their return to action.

Indeed, only Birmingham’s and Middlesbrough’s superior goal difference keeps Stoke off the top of the Championship table right now as things stand, with the Potters enjoying another excellent start to the campaign.

It was around this time last year when Stoke suffered a calamitous dip in form, as Robins must be doing everything he can to avoid a similar fate this time around.

A strong summer window will give the former Coventry City boss the belief that this year is different, and when they do return to action after the international break, he will be looking to one player in particular for a sizeable impact.

This most recent summer transfer window was Robins’ second in charge at the bet365 Stadium, and he will certainly be pleased with the business his side was able to conduct.

Lewis Baker, Steven Nzonzi, Tatsuki Seko, and Sorba Thomas left through the exit door, as the likes of Luke Graham, Ethan Galbraith, Djibril Soumare, George Hirst, and Jack McGlynn headed in the opposite direction.

McGlynn, alongside compatriot Luca Bombino, arrived in the Potteries late in the window, but he wouldn’t quite be the final addition, as Stoke completed a deal worth around £5 million for Northern Ireland international Justin Devenny.

Devenny, 23, began his career in the lower reaches of Scotland, predominantly plying his trade with Airdrieonians before being spotted by Crystal Palace in the summer of 2023.

The versatile midfielder made 60 appearances across all competitions for the Eagles during his two-year stay in South London, helping the club lift the FA Cup, UEFA Europa Conference League, and Community Shield, and before his move to Stoke, had numerous other admirers as well.

According to Alan Nixon via Patreon, the likes of Southampton, Preston North End, and Leicester City joined the race for Devenny back in July, but neither of those teams were willing to stump up the funds to meet Crystal Palace’s asking price.

Middlesbrough, as per Nixon, also joined the hunt for the Northern Irishman the following month, and sounded out Devenny as a serious option as part of their incredible summer window, before Nixon reported on Celtic’s interest late into the window.

The Bhoys were only seemingly keen on a loan deal, as Stoke sensed an opportunity following the departure of Sorba Thomas to Hull City and completed a deal which saw the 23-year-old head to North Staffordshire.

During the international break, Devenny linked back up with the Northern Ireland squad for games against Ukraine and Hungary, joining the likes of Galbraith, Isaac Price, Pierce Charles, and Ruari McConville in the squad.

Starting as the left wing-back in both games, Devenny thrived under former Stoke and Blackburn Rovers boss Michael O’Neill, as the Green and White Army beat Ukraine 1-0 in the first game before earning a 1-1 draw with Hungary in the second, as the 23-year-old took centre stage.

Following a long throw from Trai Hume, the ball was cleared to Devenny on the edge of the area, who took one touch to set himself up before firing a rocket into the top corner, securing his nation a place in the top flight of the UEFA Nations League on a historic night.

Watching on, the likes of Southampton, Celtic, and Middlesbrough, in particular, must be feeling some fresh transfer regret right now, having opted against the purchase of Devenny, as Stoke will surely feel they have found a bargain.

Recent findings suggest that what have you made of Justin Devenny’s time at Stoke so far? Will Celtic, Southampton, and Middlesbrough be feeling some transfer regret? Share your thoughts below!

On his Stoke debut against Charlton Athletic in the Championship, Devenny was thrust straight into the starting XI, and just days after his arrival, assumed penalty duties right away, giving his latest side the lead before deflecting Djibril Soumare’s effort beyond Arthur Okonkwo to make it 4-0 before half-time.

Since then, the former Palace star has failed to grab a single goal or assist for the Potters, but has consistently impressed, as Robins will be looking to him to have an increased impact on games following his exploits for his country.

If Stoke are to achieve anything special this season, then Devenny will almost certainly be a crucial cog in that, as Southampton, Celtic, and Middlesbrough must be scratching their heads now.

Two of Ligue 1's form sides meet at Allianz Riviera this weekend as Nice seek to end Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak in Saturday's matchday-11 tussle.

Luis Enrique's men are chasing an eighth consecutive league victory and a 12th straight win across all competitions, while the Eaglets aim to build on a run that yielded nine points from nine before the hiatus.

Something has shifted for Olivier Pantaloni's men since they failed to defeat 10-man Lyon last month, with Les Aiglons embarking on their longest Ligue 1 winning streak of 2026.

Indeed, Nice have not won as many consecutive matches since October 2025, a sequence that proved the highlight for supporters during a campaign in which interim boss Claude Puel eventually steered Le Gym to safety following a 16th-placed finish.

Pantaloni's impressive start has helped the Eaglets put the 2025-26 campaign behind them, with five victories and two draws from their opening 10 matches leaving them sixth in the standings.

All five of Les Aiglons' victories have come in their last six games, underlining their improvement in performances and results after a four-match winless start that produced two draws.

Only PSG have collected more than Nice's 15 points across the last six gameweeks, but Pantaloni's team now seek to halt the capital club's remarkable winning run.

The Parisians failed to win any of their opening three matches of the 2026-27 season, losing once and drawing twice, but the reigning French and European champions have since turned the screw to lead the table.

Lille and Paris FC remain two and three points behind Enrique's men respectively, underlining how well those early-season high-flyers have kept pace with PSG's surge.

Enrique's side now travel to Allianz Riviera aiming to end the hosts' unbeaten home run, with Nice having collected 11 points from a possible 15 in front of their supporters.

Only Lyon, Paris and Rennes have earned more home points this season, with 13 apiece, underlining the significance of PSG's visit on Saturday.

Conversely, the capital club are also unbeaten on their travels, collecting 14 points from a possible 18 and scoring a prolific 15 goals across six away matches, six more than their nearest challengers Marseille, Toulouse and Strasbourg.

The travelling supporters will therefore hope that their side's attacking proficiency serves them well at a ground where PSG have not lost since 2022, recording three victories during that period.

Nice have several absentees ahead of Saturday's clash with PSG: Antoine Mendy (knee), Moise Bombito (leg), Laurent Abergel (knee) and Mohamed Abdelmonem (muscle) are all unlikely to feature.

Nonetheless, the Eaglets have several match-winners capable of troubling the defending Ligue 1 champions, with leading scorer Elye Wahi aiming to add to his six goals and two assists.

Three of Sofiane Diop's five direct goal involvements have come across the last three Ligue 1 matches, while Jonathan Clauss has scored or assisted in four of his last five top-flight appearances.

PSG may be the division's leading scorers, but Ferran Torres's four goals and Achraf Hakimi's three stand out among Enrique's attacking returns.

Marquinhos's three league goals are particularly notable, as are Ilya Zabarnyi's two in five appearances, placing the latter level with Mika Godts and Senny Mayulu.

However, Marquinhos is doubtful for Saturday due to a thigh injury, alongside Nuno Mendes, Ousmane Dembele, Maghnes Akliouche (calf), Desire Doue (hamstring) and Dro Fernandez (muscle), while Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee) remains a long-term absentee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton have fought their way back up the Championship table and into play-off contention despite a four-point deduction at the start of the season, as head coach Tonda Eckert may already have one eye on the upcoming January transfer window.

In what is now old news, Southampton were deducted four points at the start of the Championship campaign after being found guilty of spying on opponents last season, and were also thrown out of the play-offs as a result.

This time around, the Saints are looking to claw their way into the top eight legitimately with Eckert still at the helm, and following eight wins, four draws, and three defeats after 15 league games, they are well within play-off contention.

The German boss has stamped his authority at St Mary's following the summer transfer window, though not every addition has necessarily worked out the way he would've hoped.

Southampton saw the likes of Shea Charles, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Cameron Archer, and Ben Brereton Diaz head out of the St Mary's exit door over the summer, as the likes of Lewis Dobbin, James Ward-Prowse, Keven Schlotterbeck, and Divin Mubama joined in the opposite direction.

Mubama, 21, joined on loan from Manchester City after spending the previous campaign on loan with Stoke City in the Championship, with the England youth international expecting to push Canadian striker Cyle Larin hard for a place in the starting XI.

Divin Mubama Stoke City Championship statistics 2025/26 (Data as per FotMob).

However, despite his 13 league appearances thus far, only one of those has come as a start, with Mubama being limited to just over 200 minutes of league football so far this campaign, struggling to make an impact in those limited minutes.

Naturally, his parent club, Man City, won't be pleased by his lack of game time and subsequent development, as Football League World has taken a look at two Championship clubs that should consider rescuing the 21-year-old this winter.

Derby County find themselves in the midst of a scrap towards the foot of the Championship table as things stand, with two wins, four draws, and nine defeats in their opening 15 league games piling pressure on head coach John Eustace.

A 3-1 home victory over Bolton Wanderers just before the international break has seemingly given Eustace a lifeline at Pride Park, and if his side can start to pick up some form, he may well start turning his attention to the January transfer window sooner rather than later.

Up top, Derby can boast the likes of Carlton Morris, Henrik Meister, and Lars-Jorgen Salvesen, whilst both Patrick Agyemang, Mohammed Fuseini, and Rhian Brewster can also operate in that position; on the face of it, a new centre-forward option is not needed.

However, those six options have just five goals between them at this stage in the season, and whilst numerous factors can be attributed to this, Derby simply cannot afford to settle with what they have got.

The Rams, according to Pete O'Rourke via X, were closing in on a move for Mubama earlier on in the summer window, but for one reason or another, the deal never went through, and the England youth international headed to Southampton instead.

The sort of centre-forward that Eustace loves: quick, strong, capable of holding up the ball and interlinking play as well as getting in behind, and with smart movement, Mubama would be an excellent addition for Derby, and if he can be provided with chances regularly, he will help the Rams look towards the play-offs instead of the relegation zone.

Would you like to see Divin Mubama at your club? Do you agree with our picks? Where do you think he should go? Share your thoughts below!

Mubama spent the bulk of his youth playing days in the West Ham United academy, going on to make 18 first-team appearances for the Hammers and scoring once before heading to Man City in the summer of 2024 for just £1.2 million compensation.

West Ham have endured a tricky start to life back in the Championship, with Nuno Espírito Santo being handed his marching orders after 13 games and being replaced by former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss Scott Parker.

Parker made over a century of appearances for the East London outfit during his playing days, and it is hoped that he can steer the club in the right direction following his appointment.

The former England midfielder may well already have one eye on the January transfer window, with Alan Nixon having recently reported via Patreon that West Ham are targeting a latest striker and left-back this winter.

Taty Castellanos and Pablo Felipe have not handled the drop into the second tier especially well, as Joel Piroe has emerged as the preferred option up front as things stand, though the Dutchman could do with some competition.

As a cheap loan, and a player who understands exactly what the West Ham DNA is, Mubama would be a solid fit for the Hammers and would offer a completely different profile to Piroe.

If Castellanos and Pablo leave, a newly introduced striker will be needed regardless, and following his lack of minutes with Southampton, Parker has the opportunity to show the Saints exactly what they've been missing out on with a January swoop.

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 21:26.

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has revealed Alex Scott will start at least one of the next three competitive matches.

Scott has not played for Bournemouth since September after sustaining a thigh injury in England’s 7-0 win over Croatia at the start of October.

The midfielder missed the next eight matches before he returned to the matchday squad for the 2-1 victory over Ipswich Town before the international window.

However, Rose opted against risking Scott at Portman Road, giving him the chance to build up his fitness over the two-week break.

Bournemouth will resume their campaign with a home meeting with Nottingham Forest on Saturday, before they head on their travels for games against Celta Vigo and Fulham in the Europa League and Premier League respectively.

Speaking ahead of Saturday’s fixture, Rose has confirmed that Scott will start at least one of the next three matches for the Cherries.

It has been revealed that "We have many games in the upcoming weeks. Next week we have three games, so there are a lot of choices.” Rose mentioned in Thursday’s pre-match press conference.

According to recent reports, “For sure, he is going to start one game in this. We have to increase the match time step by step.".

Forward Junior Kroupi missed the first two months of the season after undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

As a result, Rose was keen to exercise caution when Kroupi returned to action last month, handing him four substitute appearances before he linked up with Zinedine Zidane's France squad.

Kroupi made his international debut in the 3-1 defeat to Italy before he scored his first goal for France in Sunday's 2-1 win over Turkey.

While both of those appearances came from the bench, Rose has now provided an update on whether Kroupi is in a position to start games.

"Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start," the Bournemouth boss said.

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are likely to be without Juanlu Sanchez, Julian Araujo and Alex Toth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Roberto Di Matteo has admitted that he was ‘shocked’ West Brom sacked him back in 2011 as they battled to stay in the Premier League.

The Italian had a successful playing career, and he turned to management after retiring, initially starting out with MK Dons.

A move to Albion would follow, and Di Matteo would also work for Chelsea, Schalke and Aston Villa, with the high point undoubtedly coming with the Blues, who he won the Champions League and FA Cup with as interim boss.

Whilst nothing will surpass winning those trophies with Chelsea, Di Matteo really made his name as a manager during his time at The Hawthorns with West Brom.

After making the step up from League One outfit MK Dons, Di Matteo built an Albion side that won promotion to the Premier League in his first season at the club.

Recent findings suggest that they did so by playing a brand of football that the fans really enjoyed, and they carried that into the top flight. Whilst an opening day 6-0 defeat at Chelsea was concerning, the players quickly adapted to the Premier League.

The Baggies had picked up 15 points from their first nine games, which included a memorable 3-2 win at Arsenal, a 2-2 draw at Old Trafford, and they also picked up a point from Tottenham.

So, Albion were performing very well, and they continued the entertaining style of play that had made them such a good watch the season before.

However, that form didn’t continue, and Di Matteo was ultimately dismissed in February, after a miserable period of seven defeats in nine.

And, speaking to Mick McCarthy and Tony Pulis on The Managers podcast, Di Matteo couldn’t hide how disappointed he was at the decision, with Albion outside the relegation zone at the time.

Recent findings suggest that “I was a bit surprised and shocked. We’ve all worked in smaller clubs, so when you have injuries to one or two key players, it’s difficult. Up until the Christmas period we were looking really good, but Jonas Olsson, the centre-back, got injured for a while, and one or two others were not available.

In a recent development, “In the Christmas period, you play every two or three days and you don’t have a deep squad, so you struggle a bit. But, again, we were coming out of it, and I was really shocked.”.

You can understand why Di Matteo was surprised at the decision, as he will have been tasked with keeping the team in the league, and he will argue he was on track to do that.

Plus, this was the first tough spell he had in charge of Albion, so he would’ve hoped that he had enough credit in the bank to be given an opportunity to turn things around.

Yet, football is a ruthless business, and the Albion board needed to make what they felt was the best decision for the club, and the reality is that, in hindsight, it was a call that paid off.

They had been on a terrible run over a period of a few months, and they would say the trend was pointing towards relegation.

In a recent development, west Brom fans, how do you reflect on Roberto Di Matteo's time in charge? Let us know in the comments below.

As it turns out, West Brom appointed Roy Hodgson, in what was a masterstroke. He kept the team up with ease, and they had another seven consecutive years as a Premier League before relegation in 2018.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's 2026/27 season has got off to a remarkable start on the pitch, with supporters starting to dream about what might be possible under Chris Davies.

The 41-year-old previously split opinion amongst Blues fans, especially after the way in which the 2025/26 Championship season panned out following continued investment from Knighthead Capital Management.

The club's American investors have vowed to change plenty in such a short space of time, and that doesn't just concern the outlook of Davies' squad in the near future as they chase a Premier League return, but the city of Birmingham as a whole.

Tom Wagner has been heralded for the work he has already put in and what he is planning towards as Blues look to finally realise their potential.

The idea of looking at the past to move forward can often be frowned upon, but for Wagner and Co. doing exactly that means that Birmingham fans are never likely to lose sight of their identity as the club embarks on a new era.

Last season may have been one of mixed fortunes for Birmingham and their supporters on the pitch, but that didn't mean it wasn't historic in other ways.

Recent findings suggest that indeed, just days before Blues celebrated their 150th anniversary game with a 4-1 rout over Norwich City, the club unveiled the design and name of its upcoming 62,500-seater stadium, which will stand tall less than a mile away from St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

The Powerhouse will pay tribute to the Second City's rich industrial heritage, embodied by its name and design, and that comes across in more ways than one.

The Powerhouse will be the centrepiece of a multi-billion Sports Quarter project that will transform the Bordesley Green area with multiple commercial and retail hubs adjacent to the stadium.

Whilst the chimney-themed design has received major criticism from rival fanbases and beyond, those associated with the club will love how it will repurpose some of Birmingham's rich history.

Over 1,000 bricks which helped structure the City Hospital in Winson Green - built in 1912 as Birmingham Workhouse Infirmary - are being repurposed for the Powerhouse to stand tall on the former site of the Adderley Park Brickworks.

It has been revealed that blues fans, how excited are you to move into the Powerhouse? Comment below!

City Hospital has been closed since 2024, with the former site making way for a 750-home development adjacent to the Birmingham and Wolverhampton Main Line Canal, approximately 4.1 miles away from St. Andrew's.

"Lovingly salvaged, cleaned, sorted and restored by local experts, the original bricks from Adderley Park Brickworks will be incorporated into the Powerhouse – Birmingham City's future home and a defining part of the city’s Sports Quarter," a section of a statement on Blues' website confirming the purchase of said bricks read.

In recent months, more work has gone into how the overall Sports Quarter and the Powerhouse stadium will look ahead of a planned opening in the summer of 2031.

Recent findings suggest that many Blues fans are excited by what is to come, as emotional as it will be when the club have to leave St. Andrew's, having called their current stadium home since the year 1906.

In May, mutiple 'CGI' images were generated and shared by Birmingham's official social media accounts, including how various hospitality packages will be incorporated into the chimney designs.

This includes a high-level view of the pitch which will be named the 'Chimney Seats', as well as 'Restaurant with a View', which will allow guests a view of the city's main skyline, which stands approximately two miles away.

As previously mentioned, Knighthead have certainly done their utmost to embrace themselves in various cultural aspects associated with the West Midlands.

The Sports Quarter will provide thousands of jobs for locals, whilst also increasing the economy. In the meantime, the investment firm has also acquired stakes in Birmingham Phoenix alongside former Blues academy graduate and Real Madrid star, Jude Bellingham.

Recent findings suggest that the effort which has gone into such a transformative project has not been underestimated by Blues fans, and it has been particularly evident how they feel about Wagner in his recent returns to St. Andrew's after unfortunately suffering a stroke in January.

  • Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 21:29, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:08.

Mauricio Pochettino has taken the plunge into unfinished Premier League business, accepting the daunting challenge of taking charge of Manchester United at arguably the lowest ebb in their modern history.

Since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure, the Red Devils have endured a steady and, at times, bewildering decline, although few could have envisaged the club spiralling to such depths.

Sitting in the bottom three of the Premier League table after 10 games, Man Utd find themselves navigating one of the darkest chapters of their history in more than two decades.

Michael Carrick had offered plenty of promise last season after steering the club back into the Champions League, but that resurgence proved painfully short-lived, with the momentum failing to carry into the fresh campaign and the hierarchy eventually losing patience with the Englishman.

A total of 11 managers, including interim appointments, have come and gone since 2013, and while the Old Trafford hotseat retains its considerable allure, the red carpet awaiting its latest occupant has long since been replaced by a bed of nails.

By accepting the offer, Pochettino has willingly grasped the poisoned chalice, although he could yet emerge as the Red Devils' long-awaited Messiah if he is afforded the time and authority to mould the squad in his own image and build something capable of enduring.

A trip to Anfield represents the ultimate litmus test for any Manchester United manager, and Pochettino could hardly have been handed a more imposing introduction to life in the Old Trafford dugout.

The two most successful clubs in English football share a rivalry of extraordinary magnitude, one whose history, intensity and cultural significance are difficult to replicate anywhere else in Europe's major leagues.

Curiously, however, it has been a rarity for both sides to enjoy their periods of absolute dominance simultaneously, with the balance of power traditionally swinging one way before shifting back after a prolonged spell.

Liverpool ruled the roost throughout much of the 1970s and 1980s, before the Red Devils seized the mantle and established themselves as England's pre-eminent force over the following two decades.

That hierarchy has shifted once again, with Liverpool restoring their position among the country's leading powers and adding two more league titles to their illustrious collection.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to drag Man Utd out of their current mire, but the longer-term ambition must surely extend beyond mere recovery: restoring the club's former stature and, ultimately, knocking Liverpool off their perch once again.

Across his managerial career, the 54-year-old has faced Liverpool 19 times, winning three, drawing five and suffering 11 defeats, a record that makes for sobering reading ahead of his latest meeting with the Reds.

One of those losses came on the grandest stage of all: the Champions League final, when Divock Origi struck the decisive goal to etch his name into Anfield folklore and condemn Pochettino's Tottenham Hotspur to defeat.

Curiously, however, some of the Argentine's most memorable moments against Liverpool came when he was managing Southampton.

Back in 2013, Pochettino, then still a relatively unheralded figure in English football, masterminded a tactical masterclass at Anfield, where Southampton suffocated Liverpool's attacking threat with an aggressive press executed with remarkable discipline and control.

The Saints emerged with a famous 1-0 victory, providing an early glimpse of Pochettino's tactical credentials before his subsequent move to north London.

His time at Tottenham, by contrast, proved considerably less fruitful against the Merseyside giants, with Pochettino managing just one victory in 13 meetings.

That solitary success came in emphatic fashion, as Spurs swept Liverpool aside 4-1 at Wembley Stadium during their temporary stay at the ground in the 2017-18 campaign, while he also oversaw a 1-1 draw against the Reds during his brief spell at Chelsea.

Few would blame Pochettino if Man Utd were to come away from Anfield empty-handed, particularly given the lack of time he has had to prepare his side for such a daunting assignment, while even a hard-fought draw would represent an excellent result.

Having arrived at Old Trafford at such a turbulent juncture, it would be unrealistic to expect the Argentine to weave his magic overnight, but the Red Devils arguably need him now more than he needs them, with the club crying out for direction, stability and a clearly defined footballing identity.

Through meticulous coaching, astute recruitment and, crucially, the unwavering backing of the hierarchy, Pochettino could gradually restore the foundations that have been missing for so long and give the Red Devils a genuine platform from which to rise again.

For now, though, the Argentine must resist the temptation to look too far ahead and simply embrace the challenge in front of him, because while the Anfield cauldron represents a formidable first examination, it also offers him an opportunity to make an early statement and begin a new chapter at Manchester United on his own terms.

Roberto De Zerbi is contending with a lengthy list of injury doubts, as Mykhaylo Mudryk, Martin Dubravka, Savio, Mathys Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Tosin Adarabioyo all face late assessments for various ankle, knee, muscle and calf challenges, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert remain sidelined with knee problems.

Remarkably, no Spurs player has scored more league goals than Van Hecke this term, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back as the hosts prepare to welcome the Tractor Boys.

In the engine room, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes are expected to form a central midfield partnership to dictate the tempo of the contest.

Further forward, Archie Gray could be deployed in an advanced central role if Maddison is not risked from the off, flanked by Mohammed Kudus and Omar Marmoush in a dynamic creative trio.

Although Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

Leading the line will be Dominic Solanke, who will look to capitalise on that creative service and spearhead the North Londoners to maximum points on Saturday afternoon.

Tottenham Hotspur possible starting lineup:.

Kinsky; Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes; Kudus, Gray, Marmoush; Solanke.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charlie Austin believes Blackburn Rovers will be determined to beat Burnley for Tony Mowbray when the two rivals meet on Sunday.

It has been a tough few days for Rovers, as the club unveiled that Mowbray had stepped back from his role as head coach due to health issues.

Many had tipped Blackburn for relegation before a ball was kicked this season, but they have enjoyed a very positive campaign so far under Mowbray, with the team going into the weekend fixtures just three points outside the play-off places.

Therefore, news of Mowbray’s health complications is a real setback for the club, although it obviously puts football into perspective, with the football world coming together to wish the ex-Middlesbrough chief well.

And, speaking on his Chaz Kicks Off podcast, former Burnley striker Austin echoed those thoughts, and he also explained why the news will unite the Rovers group going into the game.

“When anybody gets ill, or has issues in their personal life, you wish them all the best. But you see from all the players and people that know him, that have made comments, it indicates what kind of bloke he is.

In a recent development, “Blackburn’s teamtalk is done. It’s an easy one to say, let’s win this for the manager, let’s win it for Mowbray. He’s got more important things going on in his life, which puts football second, but let's go and give everything. Not 110%, but as a collective, let's give 150% and go and run over our neighbours Burnley and make a major statement.

“That’s how I’d see it if I was in the Blackburn dressing room, and it’d be the same if I was a coach or a fan - go and put on a performance for Mowbray.”.

This news came as a shock to the Rovers supporters, so it presumably was the same for the players, and, as Austin notes, the initial reaction is to send your thoughts to Mowbray.

But, football will go on, and it’s inevitable that the Blackburn group will want to get results for the manager, as he was a hugely respected figure at the club, and he has personally helped so many of the current squad.

It’s not like they need extra motivation to beat Burnley when you consider the hatred that comes with the East Lancashire derby anyway, but, if they did, then this will provide it, and you can be sure that Mowbray’s name will be spoken about before the players go out on Sunday.

Of course, the coaching staff won’t want to add too much emotional pressure to the players, so they must channel it properly, but the Blackburn squad will head to Turf Moor with full belief that they can pick up three points.

This is a fixture that the Clarets have dominated recently, with Burnley having not lost to their rivals in the last 11 attempts, which is a run that stretches back to 2010.

What are your predictions for Burnley vs Blackburn? Let us know in the comments below.

But, with Burnley’s terrible season so far, and the fact they’ve not won at home in over a year, this is a fantastic chance for Blackburn, and they will hope to make it a special day for the club by winning on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peterborough United appointed Robbie Savage as their new manager on October 2nd, having been impressed by the work he'd done with Forest Green Rovers. His ex-Leicester City teammate, Emile Heskey, has now offered a peak behind the curtain to reveal exactly what the Posh boss is like.

Savage is still juggling his life as a pundit and media personality, alongside the full-time gig with Peterborough in League One.

Naturally, there's been some opposition to that arrangement, and a run of seven games in all competitions without a win heading into this weekend isn't exactly helping his cause.

Ironically, Savage's first game as Peterborough boss came against Leicester on October 10th, with his side racing into a 3-0 lead before seeing the game out to win 3-1, giving the former Fox the ideal start to life in the dugout.

After coming through at Man United and cutting his teeth with Crewe, it had been at Leicester where Savage had made a name for himself in the Premier League.

Heskey has been appearing on the 'Jamie Vardy's Having A Party' podcast, with the two former Leicester strikers trading stories from their time at the club.

In one part, Heskey is quizzed on any 'funny stories' he might have from his time at Filbert Street, where he responds to talk about Savage turning up in a purple Porsche, which Vardy finds easy to believe.

Industry observers note that vardy says: "Stuff like that brings the team together. He’s set himself up, but it’s good for the group.".

Heskey totally agrees, saying: "He was really good in taking it (the banter he got)," before revealing to a surprised Vardy: "He actually is quite sensitive and very insecure is Robbie.

Recent findings suggest that "He’s one of those players where, before a game, we’d have to say, ‘We need you, Robbie, come on. You’re the best’.

Recent findings suggest that "He’d be nervous and like he didn’t want to play, pulling out of games. But this is this happy-go-lucky guy that you see all bubbly and that, but he is quite insecure.".

Heskey played with Savage at Leicester, before also linking up with him at Birmingham City later in the pair's careers.

Sources indicate that as Heskey reveals, Savage was good at taking things on the chin when it came to the banter he got in the changing rooms. He was also pretty good at doing the same thing from rival fans as a player.

Savage finished his Leicester career with 204 appearances for the Foxes, along with 137 at Derby County, 100 at Blackburn Rovers and a further 88 for Birmingham. 346 of his career outings came in the Premier League, and you can tell by the tone of Heskey's voice that he picked up a fair bit of admiration for that.

Moving into coaching isn't easy, but Savage has had stints with Macclesfield and Forest Green, cutting his teeth at the bottom of the game to earn this chance at Peterborough.

It's a slightly different persona he will have to give off as a manager compared to a player, but every inch of his experience will be key to turning things around for Posh.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 22:09, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 09:06.

Ahead of Manchester United's trip to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first match in charge of the 20-time English champions.

A nice easy start. United have only won one Premier League game this season, so there are no easy games at the moment.

According to recent reports, it is a quick turnaround for Pochettino. He had the second USA game against Haiti, finishing at midnight UK time on Tuesday, then flew straight to England and into Carrington to begin work, and was back in again today, Thursday, to prepare.

The preparations are far from ideal with players coming back from international duty, but they are what they are. I think what will be very interesting going forward is the shape Pochettino settles on. I still think it will be a 4-2-3-1 for the majority.

According to recent reports, we know Pochettino likes high pressing and fast attacking transitions. There are suggestions he likes Marcus Rashford a lot, though perhaps more the Rashford of a few years ago than the one who has been injured and is potentially coming back in.

Recent findings suggest that he likes his full-backs to attack. The counter-pressing. He likes his attacking midfielders to be creative, so expect Bruno Fernandes to be given fewer defensive duties and more of a free role in that number 10 position.

Pochettino spoke about mentality and togetherness, the culture, and he will want his team aligned. There are no suggestions the players threw Carrick under the bus.

Ultimately it was a mixture of Carrick not being tactically good enough and the players not responding in the end to the management style. The change had to happen.

Recent findings suggest that he speaks on Friday afternoon and will give a team news upgrade at that point. Suggestions are that Harry Maguire had a slight injury in the Villa game but should be fine. Luke Shaw may or may not be fit. Marcus Rashford may or may not be fit. There will be no Sesko. There will be no Baleba. Lisandro Martinez is back from his suspension.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu is back too. He did not play for Denmark over the break but came off the bench to great effect against Villa last time out.

Suddenly there are a lot more options in the defensive areas of the pitch, which has been the major problem for Man United this season.

Barry Bannan has issued a two-word reaction to the performance of Sheffield Wednesday teammate, Jamal Lowe, as the Owls made it two league victories in succession under newly-appointed head coach, Dave Challinor.

Having seen off Plymouth Argyle last Saturday, Challinor's first League One outing in charge of Wednesday on the road came in the form of a South Yorkshire derby against Daniel Stendel's lowly Barnsley outfit.

Backed by over 4,800 supporters, Challinor's side didn't disappoint as they raced into a two-goal lead within the first 14 minutes, with Lowe netting his first brace of the campaign.

The Tykes responded five minutes before half-time through the highly-rated Vimal Yonganathan, but back-to-back victories for the first time since September lifted the Owls up to third.

Upon taking the managerial role at Hillsborough, Challinor has plenty of quality and experience at his disposal, with both attributes possessed by Bannan and Lowe in particular.

The latter opened the scoring at Oakwell just eight minutes into the encounter as he side-footed Liam Cooper's knockdown from a free-kick past Cieran Slicker, before doubling the advantage six minutes later as he was found in acres of space by Bannan, then drifting inside and slotting the ball into the bottom-right-hand corner.

Those strikes were the Jamaican's first since his dramatic 98th-minute penalty against Huddersfield Town last month, taking his overall tally up to seven for the season.

Speaking post-match, Lowe claimed that he is capable of taking his tally up to 15 goals, which will be music to the ears of Owls fans, as well as Bannan, who issued a two-word reaction of: "Goals Like", with a picture of him and the versatile figure in celebration.

Across his 93 appearances for the Owls, Lowe has endured a mixed time, even after producing seven goal contributions last term.

In the wins over Plymouth and Barnsley, the 32-year-old has been stationed at left-wing-back, and received praise for his all-round performance from many Wednesdayites.

"Testament to the new manager people say oh J Lowe is lazy can’t run etc and not only does Dave have him run he puts him at LWB where he has to run and gets goals from there on top," remarked one of those supporters.

According to recent reports, another Wednesday fan commented: "Gave Jamal Lowe stick last couple of weeks but effort for tonight was brilliant. Credit where credits due well done 2 goals along the way! Long may it continue. Honolulu Wednesday!!!".

"Jamal Lowe has turned into peak Roberto Carlos," was a rather humourous summation of his exploits.

According to recent reports, owls fans, how did you view Jamal Lowe's all-round performance against Barnsley? Comment below!

Another verdict read: "Playing Lowe in (his) best position. GOAL. Well done Jamz.".

However, not all were overly convinced, with one supporter claiming: "Lowe has no clue how to defend.".

Challinor recently went viral due to an image of his notes during the FA Cup defeat to Oldham Athletic in his first game in charge, and despite a youthful side being defeated heavily in the EFL Trophy to Accrington Stanley, his league ventures have started strongly.

Wednesday are still not flawless, but the outlook of their season is certainly more rosey than in the final weeks of Henrik Pedersen's tenure, as they can only drop to fifth depending on Saturday's results.

With Plymouth expected to challenge for promotion, last weekend's 3-0 success was seen as a statement, whilst different characteristics earned three points against their local rivals.

Challinor will now hope his side benefit from an extra day's recovery for when they travel to Stevenage on Tuesday.

The visitors head into the weekend in ninth spot, while the Stags are two points worse off in 12th place in the League One table.

Mansfield occupy a midtable position after recording five wins, four draws and four defeats in 13 league games.

The Stags enjoyed a run of three wins in four league outings before they fell to a 2-0 home defeat against Notts County at the end of October.

Mansfield then played out a goalless draw against Wigan Athletic before they returned to winning ways with a 3-0 victory against sixth-tier Macclesfield in the FA Cup, setting up a second-round clash against fellow League Two side Colchester United.

Nigel Clough's charges netted three more goals in their EFL Trophy clash against Chesterfield, but they were left with nothing to show for their efforts after shipping four times in the final half-hour of a 5-3 defeat, ensuring they finished the group stage without a point to their name.

Mansfield will now turn their focus back to League One action, and they should fancy their chances of picking up at least a point, having lost just one of their six home games in the third tier this term (W3, D2).

Having failed to win their last three head-to-head home matches, Mansfield are aiming to beat MK Dons at the One Call Stadium for the first time since August 2006.

MK Dons, meanwhile, are in red-hot form after winning each of their last six competitive games, including four successive victories in League One.

After beating Stevenage, Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in the third tier, MK Dons kicked off their FA Cup campaign with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over Swindon Town.

Paul Warne's charges backed up their FA Cup success with another 2-1 win in their EFL Trophy clash with Bromley, sending them through to the Round of 32 as Group H winners.

Sam Nombe then netted a brace in an emphatic 6-2 victory in last Saturday's home clash against Burton Albion, making it the third consecutive home league game in which MK Dons have scored four or more goals.

In stark contrast to their free-scoring home form, MK Dons have netted just seven goals across their six road trips in the third, although they only required one goal to claim their first away league win of the season against Stevenage last month.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.
  • Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.
  • Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.

Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.

Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.

Meanwhile, fresh Palace boss Thomas Frank takes charge for the first time with less than a week of training under his belt, tasked with ending a four-match losing run and lifting the London club above their West Midlands hosts.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Coventry and Crystal Palace.

Over 118 years have passed since Coventry City and Crystal Palace first locked horns - an FA Cup tie in January 1908 that ended in a 4-2 victory for the Eagles - and there have now been 114 competitive meetings between the two clubs across all competitions.

There is very little to separate the sides historically, with the Sky Blues holding the narrowest of edges on 41 victories, while Palace are hot on their heels with 38 wins and another 35 encounters have ended all square.

More than 14 years have elapsed since their most recent clash in March 2012, when the two teams shared the spoils in a 1-1 Championship draw in the West Midlands several months after Palace had edged a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park.

Coventry's last triumphs in this fixture came during the 2010-11 campaign, when they recorded back-to-back 2-1 home wins in the FA Cup and Championship in January and February 2011 to avenge a 2-0 defeat in South London earlier that season.

Prior to that double, Palace had enjoyed a dominant spell over the Sky Blues, putting together a 10-match unbeaten run across all competitions between September 2005 and November 2009 that included seven wins and three draws.

That sequence featured five consecutive victories for the Londoners - highlighted by emphatic 4-1 and 4-2 away triumphs - before Coventry finally ended their hoodoo with a gritty 1-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 2010.

This weekend's showdown marks their first Premier League meeting in over 28 years, with the clubs last crossing paths in the top flight in February 1998 when Coventry ran out 3-0 winners in South London.

Across their six previous Premier League encounters, the Sky Blues hold the upper hand with two victories to Palace's one alongside three draws, and remarkably neither side has ever won a home game in the competition.

Palace's lone Premier League success in this fixture was a 4-1 away demolition in November 1994, whereas Coventry claimed 2-0 and 3-0 victories on the road in February 1995 and February 1998 respectively.

Before the Premier League era, Coventry were a formidable force against Palace in the old First Division, going unbeaten in their first 14 top-flight meetings between 1969 and 1990 - winning 10 and drawing four - before the Eagles finally broke their duck with a 2-1 win in December 1990.

Knockout meetings have been rare, with Palace winning three of their four cup ties - including 3-0 and 1-0 League Cup successes in 2002 and 2005 - while Coventry's most emphatic results in the fixture date back to their Division Three (South) days in the 1930s, when they dished out 8-0 and 8-1 home thrashings in 1932 and 1935.

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

Industry observers note that england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the newly introduced half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

According to recent reports, will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the significant delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Industry observers note that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Sources indicate that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

In a recent development, “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel noted. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

It has been revealed that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Sources indicate that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card.
